name: Botswana
tagline: A delta that never reaches the sea
summary: The Okavango empties into the Kalahari and evaporates, and the whole country is organised around that fact — low-volume, high-value safari, mokoro channels, and the salt pans of Makgadikgadi.
when: The Okavango flood peaks between June and August, months after the rain that made it.

entries.caption: A Delta That Never Reaches the Sea
entries.description: The Okavango floods into the Kalahari every year and simply disappears into it.
entries.subject: the channels and islands of the Okavango delta from the air

entries.caption: Delta, Pan and Desert
entries.description: Water in the north, salt pans in the middle, and Kalahari sand for the rest of it.
entries.subject: the Makgadikgadi salt pans stretching to the horizon

entries.caption: The Largest Elephant Population
entries.description: Chobe holds more elephant than anywhere on earth, and they come to the river at four.
entries.subject: elephants coming down to the Chobe river in late light

entries.caption: Low Volume, High Value
entries.description: Fewer beds, larger concessions, and game drives that do not meet another vehicle.
entries.subject: a game vehicle alone on a track in the Okavango

entries.caption: Tsodilo
entries.description: No real mountains — Tsodilo's four hills hold four thousand rock paintings instead.
entries.subject: the Tsodilo hills rising from flat Kalahari scrub

entries.caption: No Falls, and the Zambezi Next Door
entries.description: The water here spreads rather than drops; Victoria Falls is ninety minutes from Kasane.
entries.subject: the Chobe river spreading wide at sunset

entries.caption: The Okavango and the Chobe
entries.description: A mokoro poled through papyrus channels is the correct speed for this country.
entries.subject: a mokoro being poled through a papyrus channel

entries.caption: Landlocked
entries.description: The nearest sea is a thousand kilometres away, and nobody here seems to mind.
entries.subject: a floodplain island in the Okavango at sunrise

entries.caption: Riverine and Mopane
entries.description: Riverine forest along the Chobe, and mopane woodland across the north.
entries.subject: riverine forest along the Chobe river bank

entries.caption: Mokoro, Walking, Horseback
entries.description: Poled canoes, walking safaris on the islands, and some of the best riding safaris anywhere.
entries.subject: riders crossing a floodplain on a horseback safari

entries.caption: Batswana and San
entries.description: Setswana across the country, and San communities in the Kalahari with the oldest culture on earth.
entries.subject: a San tracker reading spoor in the Kalahari sand

entries.caption: The Kalahari San
entries.description: Tracking with San guides, who will find in an hour what nobody else sees at all.
entries.subject: San guides walking a Kalahari pan in the morning

entries.caption: Seswaa and Bogobe
entries.description: Slow-pounded beef and sorghum porridge, and braai wherever there is a fire.
entries.subject: seswaa and bogobe served at a Botswana lodge

entries.caption: Maitisong and Dithubaruba
entries.description: The Maitisong festival in Gaborone, and the Kweneng cultural festival at Dithubaruba.
entries.subject: dancers performing at a cultural festival in Botswana

entries.caption: Basketry
entries.description: Palm baskets woven in the delta panhandle, dyed with bark, and collected worldwide.
entries.subject: woven palm baskets from the Okavango panhandle

entries.caption: Tsodilo Hills
entries.description: Four thousand paintings on four hills the San call the resting place of the gods.
entries.subject: rock paintings on the Tsodilo hills

entries.caption: Diamonds and Democracy
entries.description: Independent since 1966, and the one African country that used its diamonds well.
entries.subject: the National Museum building in Gaborone

entries.caption: Maun and Kasane
entries.description: Not really cities — two safari towns with airstrips, which is what the country needs.
entries.subject: light aircraft on the apron at Maun airport

entries.caption: Tent, Deck and Sand
entries.description: Camps built on decks above the flood, taken down when the concession lease ends.
entries.subject: a tented camp on a deck above the Okavango floodplain

entries.caption: Cattle Posts
entries.description: Away from the parks the country is cattle, and the cattle post is the centre of it.
entries.subject: a cattle post at the edge of the Kalahari

entries.caption: Not the Cheapest, but Quiet
entries.description: Not a budget destination — but the children will not be sharing a sighting with ten vehicles.
entries.subject: a family on a mokoro in the Okavango channels

entries.caption: Mokoro and Walking
entries.description: Poling, walking and riding — this is the country where you get out of the vehicle.
entries.subject: walkers following a guide across an Okavango island

entries.caption: The Concession Camps
entries.description: Private concessions the size of small countries, with six tents on them.
entries.subject: a small luxury tented camp lit at dusk in the delta

entries.caption: Community Trusts
entries.description: Concessions leased through community trusts, so the villages hold the lease and the income.
entries.subject: a community conservation sign at a delta concession

entries.caption: Water and Light
entries.description: Aerial work over the delta, and reflections that only exist for the weeks of the flood.
entries.subject: aerial view of flooded Okavango channels at golden hour

entries.caption: The Makgadikgadi
entries.description: Drive onto the pan at night and there is no horizon and no sound at all.
entries.subject: quad bikes on the Makgadikgadi salt pan at dusk

entries.caption: Fewer People Than Elephants
entries.description: Two and a half million people, a hundred and thirty thousand elephant, and space for both.
entries.subject: an elephant herd crossing open Kalahari grassland
